title: Collaborative artificial intelligence for the diagnosis and management of acute ischemic stroke

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Collaborative artificial intelligence for the diagnosis and management of acute ischemic stroke》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background · abstract-1-1】Acute Ischemic Stroke (AIS) remains a critical global health challenge that requires continuous improvement in diagnostic strategies. Timely and accurate diagnosis is essential for effective reperfusion therapies such as intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy, whose clinical benefits rapidly diminish with treatment delays. Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers promising potential to enhance diagnostic accuracy and clinical decision-making in AIS. However, data fragmentation and strict privacy regulations limit the development of robust AI systems. Objectives: We aim to provide a perspective-style review that explores how collaborative AI can reshape AIS diagnostics by overcoming data access barriers, fostering cross-institutional model development, and improving diagnostic equity.

【Introduction · S0001-p1】Acute ischemic stroke (AIS), accounting for approximately 80% of all stroke cases, represents a critical challenge to global health as a leading cause of mortality, disability, and economic burden worldwide [1]. This condition, caused by an abrupt cessation of blood flow to the brain, demands immediate medical intervention due to its rapid and devastating impact on neuronal health. Within just five minutes of ischemia, brain cells begin to perish, with estimates suggesting that each minute of delayed treatment results in the loss of approximately 1.9 million neurons and 14 billion synapses [2]. Accurate and timely diagnosis is therefore vital for administering thrombolysis and thrombectomy, the two main treatment strategies for AIS, both of which are highly time-sensitive and depend on precise imaging-based decision-making [3]. Such statistics [4–6] underscore the critical importance of timely and accurate diagnosis, as well as swift decision-making, in mitigating the catastrophic effects of AIS.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Collaborative artificial intelligence for the diagnosis and management of acute ischemic stroke》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Implementations and FL platforms · S0004-p1】In the field of AIS, implementing and applying practical measures of FL involves establishing an efficient cross-institutional collaboration platform to drive the development of disease diagnosis and treatment methods. Leveraging existing FL technology and incorporating the needs of domain experts, this platform ensures knowledge sharing and model collaboration while ensuring data security and privacy protection. Initially, each participating institution establishes a secure and reliable data channel with a third-party FL platform, facilitating collaboration in data sharing and model training. Subsequently, the platform offers unified model management and services, enabling institutions to upload their models or choose from a provided model repository tailored for tasks such as ischemic stroke image recognition and clinical prediction, either as pre-trained models or optimised models under the FL framework.

【Methods · abstract-2-1】We analysed current challenges in developing AIS-related AI tools, particularly the limitations caused by restricted data sharing across healthcare institutions. The study highlights collaborative AI approaches, such as federated learning and privacy-preserving computation, which enable decentralised model training while maintaining patient confidentiality. Relevant literature and recent developments in clinical AI collaboration were reviewed.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Collaborative artificial intelligence for the diagnosis and management of acute ischemic stroke》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · S0006-p1】The application of CAI in AIS diagnosis and treatment holds great potential to transform the management of this critical condition. By enabling collaboration across multiple institutions, FL facilitates the development of robust and accurate models that enhance diagnostic precision while ensuring patient data privacy and security. FL platforms, such as FedEYE, can be customised to address the unique challenges of AIS, providing tailored solutions that consider the heterogeneous nature of patient populations, varying institutional needs, and the integration of multimodal data.

【Conclusion · S0006-p2】As FL platforms evolve, ongoing research and innovation in FL methodologies will be crucial to refining their applications in AIS and ensuring their effectiveness. Additionally, standardised guidelines and regulatory frameworks will be essential to guide the ethical and responsible implementation of FL in clinical settings. The scalability and flexibility of FL also allow smaller healthcare institutions with limited resources to participate in collaborative learning, gaining access to expert-level models and improving diagnostic capabilities without heavy computational infrastructure. Ultimately, FL’s ability to foster cross-institutional collaboration, safeguard patient privacy, and adapt to the needs of diverse healthcare institutions makes it a transformative technology poised to shape the future of AIS diagnosis and treatment.

【Figure 1. · F0001】Figure 1. The general taxonomy framework of this review. It outlines three major dimensions: Artificial Intelligence in AIS, Trustworthy Federated Learning (FL) for AIS, and Implementations and FL Platforms. Each branch corresponds to a major section in this review, progressing from clinical AI applications to trustworthy FL mechanisms and finally to practical implementation frameworks.

【Figure 2. · F0002】Figure 2. The framework of CAI for acute ischemic stroke depicts a privacy-preserving collaborative learning process. Each hospital locally trains its model on private data that never leaves its premises, while a trusted aggregation server synchronises and updates a global model through iterative parameter exchanges. This design fosters cross-institutional collaboration and shared intelligence without compromising data security or patient privacy.
